questions.question: The business cycle is:
options: The recurring rise and fall of economic activity around its long-term growth path — a wave around the trend
The steady upward trend of production over decades
The December surge in retail sales
A one-off shock such as a flood

questions.question: The PEAK of the cycle shows:
options: Production at its weakest with cheap borrowing
Activity at full stretch — factories near capacity, jobs plentiful, prices straining upward, scarce skills at a premium

questions.question: The working definition of a recession is:
options: Any month in which share prices fall
Two consecutive quarters of declining real GDP

questions.question: Saying the cycle "repeats without a timetable" means:
options: Cycles occur every five years exactly
Cycles no longer occur in modern economies
The SHAPE recurs but phases differ in length and depth every time — no clockwork

questions.question: LEADING indicators turn before the economy because they record:
options: Decisions made today about tomorrow's activity — building plans approved, new orders, confidence surveys

questions.question: Current production, retail sales and this month's employment are:
options: COINCIDENT indicators — they confirm where the economy is right now
Lagging indicators — they certify the past

questions.question: Unemployment is a LAGGING indicator because:
options: Firms retrench late and rehire late — so joblessness turns only after the economy has turned
It is measured only once a year

questions.question: The Reserve Bank's two roles in this topic are:
options: Approving building plans and vehicle sales
Compiling composite leading, coincident and lagging indicators, and officially DATING the country's cycle

questions.question: The four movements inside an economic time series are:
Retail sales leaping every December is an example of:
options: The SEASONAL movement — a calendar-driven pattern repeating within each year

questions.question: A flood collapsing one province's output for a month is classified as:
options: IRREGULAR — a one-off shock with no repeating pattern

questions.question: Statisticians publish "seasonally adjusted" figures in order to:
options: Hide bad news in weak months
Strip out the regular calendar pattern so the cycle underneath becomes visible

questions.question: EXOGENOUS causes of cycles originate:
options: OUTSIDE the economic system — drought, wars, pandemics, world commodity price swings

questions.question: Credit expanding freely in good times and tightening sharply in bad times is:
options: An ENDOGENOUS cause — it grows inside the system and amplifies the wave

questions.question: "An outside stone landing in water already sloshing" describes:
options: How real cycles usually MIX an outside shock with an inside amplifier

questions.question: In a downswing, government is squeezed from both sides because:
options: Tax revenue falls exactly when more households need support

questions.question: "More customers means more hiring means more customers" describes:
options: The upswing — breathing in, with each round feeding the next

questions.question: What quietly gathers at the TROUGH:
options: The seeds of recovery — low prices, cheaper loans, worn-out equipment queueing for replacement

questions.question: When a news anchor announces a recession, the definition in use is:
options: Falling share prices for a month
Two quarters in a row of shrinking production

questions.question: Building plans approved and new bakkie orders belong to:
options: The HEADLIGHTS — leading indicators recording today's decisions about tomorrow's activity

questions.question: This month's production and retail sales are the:
options: SPEEDOMETER — coincident indicators reading this exact moment

questions.question: "When the mirror looks darkest, the worst may already be behind you" refers to:
options: Unemployment peaking AFTER the trough — a lagging indicator

questions.question: "The composite leading indicator declined for a third straight month" translates as:
options: The economy has certainly entered a recession
The Reserve Bank has dated the trough
The nation's headlights are dimming — a warning that the turn may be coming

subtopics.title: Why the Wave Comes — and Who Gets Wet

questions.question: Iron ore prices falling on world markets and hitting Northern Cape mine towns is:
options: An OUTSIDE stone — an exogenous shock nobody local caused

questions.question: "Banks lend generously in the sunshine and call in umbrellas when it rains" describes:
options: Credit amplifying the cycle from INSIDE — endogenous, pumping peaks higher and cutting troughs deeper

questions.question: The downswing's costs fall UNEQUALLY because:
options: Retrenchments start with the last hired and least trained — the shop floor feels it before the boardroom

questions.question: Reading the cycle as self-defence means:
options: Treating every December jump as an upswing
Settling debts near the peak, holding steady near the trough, and never mistaking a season or a shock for the tide
